public_rationale: OpenAI announced improved mathematical capabilities on January 30, 2023 [e1]. A January 31 report relayed users' reports of sentence-form math failures and strong SAT math performance after the update [e2]. These selected observations do not establish how often elementary word-problem failures occurred [e2]. The systematic study's post-update tests ran in mid-February, outside the January 30–February 2 endpoint window [e3]. Together, these sources establish neither recurring failures nor dependable performance in the required window [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: No representative, reproducible evaluation covers January 30–February 2, 2023.
The original Davis examples were not recovered as complete readable transcripts.
No matched GPT-2 baseline establishes persistence of the same error classes since 2019.
The later systematic results cannot establish performance by February 2.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT hasn't really changed since 2019: its output is more fluent and lots of individual mistakes have been addressed, but more than three years on it still has a lot of problems with easy word problems, even after the late-January 2023 math update.
conditions: since 2019 / more than three years on
despite more fluent output and lots of individual mistakes addressed
even after a new update a few days ago focused around math

statement.excerpt: And GPT hasn’t really changed, either.

from_speaker: lots of individual mistakes have been addressed
even after a new update a few days ago focused around math
having lot of problems with easy word problems
our_interpretation: Read in context, this asserts persistence of frequent elementary word-problem failures despite acknowledged improvements. It does not assert that GPT made no progress.
The comparison begins with the October 2019 GPT-2 examples and ends on February 2, 2023.
The post-update component requires evidence about performance after the January 30 update and no later than the post.
A lot means recurring failures across a reasonably varied set of easy problems; isolated examples establish possibility, not frequency.
criteria.support_condition: Dated, reproducible evaluations show recurring failures on varied elementary word problems in the January 30–February 2, 2023 version, with comparable earlier failures establishing persistence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations of that post-update version show dependable performance on the relevant elementary problems, with earlier failures largely resolved across varied formulations.

evidence.excerpt: We’ve upgraded the ChatGPT model with improved factuality and mathematical capabilities.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the update referenced in the claim. It reports an intended improvement without measuring remaining word-problem failures.

evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT struggles with math equations when typed out in complete sentences instead of numbers and symbols.
evidence.explanation: The report documents post-update failure reports, but also reports strong SAT performance. These selected observations establish neither a representative failure rate nor dependable success.

evidence.excerpt: the probability of failure increases significantly when the work is not shown.
evidence.locator: Section 3, Overall Performance of ChatGPT on DRAW-1K; test timing in Section 2
evidence.explanation: The study finds substantial failures and strong sensitivity to whether work is shown. Its post-update tests ran in mid-February, so they cannot establish performance by February 2.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Archived tests of the January 30–February 2, 2023 version across varied elementary word problems, with exact prompts, responses, model identification and sampling details, plus comparable 2019 GPT-2 tests. These would need to distinguish arithmetic errors from errors interpreting events and quantities.
